The petitioner was named as the fourth accused in Annexure A1 FIR in Crime No. 514/2022 registered by the Peroorkada Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram, as against six accused persons,
for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 120B and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The Investigating Officer in the above crime has filed Annexure A2 final report before the Court of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-IV, Thiruvananthapuram, exonerating the petitioner as an accused in the crime.

sentences.text: 4. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. It is well settled that, though a person may be named as an accused in the FIR, but is not arraigned as the accused in the final report, he can no longer be branded as the accused in the crime.

6. In the present case, admittedly, though the petitioner was arraigned as the fourth accused in FIR,
the investigating officer has, in explicit terms, found that the petitioner is not involved in the crime and has not committed the above offences.

Accordingly, only the first Crl. M.C. No.1242 of 2026 -:5:
2026:KER:28265 accused has been arraigned as an accused in the above crime.
7. In light of Annexure A2 final report, I hold that Annexure A1 FIR has become redundant, as far as the petitioner is concerned.
The apprehension projected by the petitioner is unwarranted because he is no longer an accused.

In the afore-said circumstances, I close the Crl.M.C, by recording the statement of the Investigating Officer that the petitioner is not an accused in Crime No. 514/2022 registered by Peroorkada Police Station.
